feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration 7 design (best raced score 216.97: kp 3.0, ki 1.0, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, outer sensors at x = ±0.04, sensor_size 0.016, last_direction) with one change, ki from 1.0 to 1.2. All values are inside the contract limits. Integral gain is the one lever that has improved the score at every step: ki 0.4 to 0.8 gave 175.70 to 184.93 (iteration 6), and 0.8 to 1.0 gave 184.93 to 216.97 (iteration 7). Oscillation has not risen with it: s-bend steering_oscillation fell from 0.337 (iteration 6) to 0.329 (iteration 7), and the oval was 0.331, so the 0.35 limit still has some margin. Max_error stays near 0.059 to 0.063 m on every track, which fits a residual steady offset that integral action is still shrinking. Earlier evidence still argues against changing the other fields: wider outer sensors (iteration 3, 54.87), higher kp (iteration 4, 108.24) and lower base_speed (iteration 2, 115.67) all lowered the score. The main risk is integral windup: the integral is clamped at ±2, so the clamp may start to bind at this gain, and the oval finish rate (4/20 at iteration 7) could move either way. Approving this is a single-variable test with a clear fallback, and the race will show whether the trend holds. After the race, compare against 216.97 and check progress on the s-bend (target 0.46 or higher) and slalom (0.12 or higher), max_error, steering_oscillation, line_loss_events and oval completion_time. If the score falls below 216.97 with progress unchanged, keep ki 1.0 as the fallback.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation on the s-bend or oval exceeds about 0.35 in the race, return ki to 1.0 (the iteration 7 value, score 216.97) and keep kp 3.0, kd 0.5 and base_speed 1.6, since the oscillation trend is the main risk at higher ki.

If the score is at or above 216.97 with s-bend progress at or above 0.46 and slalom progress at or above 0.12, consider ki 1.4 as the next single step, with all other fields unchanged, to test whether the steady offset keeps shrinking before the integral clamp (±2) binds.
Do not change sensor positions, kp, kd or base_speed in this step. Iterations 2, 3 and 4 each lowered the score when those fields moved, and iteration 5 confirmed kd 0.5 as the best damping.
